written: 2026-11-24, by Claude; the GPU run was approved by the owner on 2026-11-24 ("the champion vs challenger GPU run on Databricks Free Edition"); the owner deploys and starts it from the laptop
items: BACKLOG items 3 (champion vs challenger) and 2 (a second registry version), as the first run of item 17's pipeline (owner, 2026-11-10)
rule: results/phase3/retrain/spec.json, unchanged: its trigger, champion, challenger recipe, held-out data, comparison and promotion rule (gain >= 2.0 points on held-out Buenos Aires with the paired 95% lower bound above 0, and client validation change >= -1.0 point)

data.challenger_training: the clients' training split plus the labelled Buenos Aires images the monthly job scored in replay months 5 to 9 (workspace.cdm.gold_prediction_audit)
data.held_out: labelled Buenos Aires images of patients (else lesions) with no image in the challenger's training data
data.client_validation: the clients' validation split (also chooses the challenger's epoch)

differences_from_the_2026_10_23_run: every challenger's checkpoints are kept and listed in challenger_models.json, promoted or not (keep_checkpoints = true)

the challenger always gets a serving bundle built and checked on CPU, in its own folder (deploy/serving/challenger-item3), and is always registered in workspace.cdm.skin_lesion_classifier with model_gen v3, decision (promoted_by_rule or rejected), decision_sha256 and serving_bundle_sha256 tags
the champion alias never moves in this job; a promotion is the owner's separate promote_challenger run, allowed only if the rule promoted
expected_outcome_note: an inference, not a result: the data, seeds and recipe match the 2026-10-23 run, which did not promote (held-out gain 6.2 points, client validation -1.6 points); a similar verdict is likely. A rejected version is registered but can never be promoted, so item 2's move to the newer version and back would still wait for a version the rule promotes
serving_bundle_test_look: serving_bundle.py's one look at the clients' test split and the two new hospitals runs for the challenger too; its Buenos Aires rows include images the challenger trained on, so they are not a held-out result
commit_after_the_run: decision.json, challenger_models.json, serving/results.json and registry/lineage.json, copied to results/phase3/challenger/ by the owner (docs/OWNER_STEPS.md)
cost: Free Edition: no charge. GPU estimate from committed records, not a result (BACKLOG item 3): about 0.7 to 1.9 GPU DBUs for a 10- to 25-minute GPU task, capped near 4.6 by the 60-minute timeout; the CPU tasks are serverless CPU
